decisions.choice: after the death of Moses: the book's setting, which picks up where Deuteronomy ends
decisions.reason: The book opens with the same words that open Judges after Joshua's death (Judges 1:1). Moses has just died on Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, Israel has mourned him for thirty days, and Joshua has been named to lead in his place (Deuteronomy 34:5-9). The people are still camped east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho. The opening "and it came about" ties this book to the story that came before it.

decisions.choice: the servant of the LORD: Moses' title as the one who belonged to God and served him
decisions.reason: The word for "servant" is the word for a slave, a person owned by a master and wholly at his disposal, not a hired worker. Said of a man and God it becomes a title of honor: the one God chose and sent to do his work. Moses is called this at his death (Deuteronomy 34:5), and the title comes back through this chapter (verses 2, 7, 13, 15). Joshua himself receives it only at his own death (24:29).

decisions.choice: attendant: a personal aide or assistant, not a slave
decisions.reason: The word here is not the word for a slave. It comes from a verb meaning "to wait on" or "to serve" a superior, and it names a trusted aide. Joshua is called this from his first years with Moses (Exodus 24:13; 33:11; Numbers 11:28). The contrast is part of the point: Moses was the LORD's servant, and Joshua, until now, was Moses' assistant.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal) / servant (Balanced, Readable) for Moses; attendant / assistant / helper for Joshua
decisions.reason: The two words are different in the Hebrew, so the English keeps them different. For Moses the title follows the usual rule: Literal shows the hard sense of the word with "slave", and Balanced and Readable say "servant", since "slave" would bring to mind modern chattel slavery rather than a title of honor. For Joshua, Literal says "attendant" as in Exodus 24:13 and 33:11, Balanced "assistant", and Readable "helper".

decisions.choice: Moses ... had died. After that, ...
decisions.reason: Readable states Moses' death as a sentence of its own before the LORD speaks, so the setting is clear.

decisions.choice: BWANA (the divine_name setting: Yahwe)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua, as in the Pentateuch: the divine name is "BWANA" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", with "Yahwe" as the reader setting. Adonai YHWH is "Bwana MUNGU (the divine_name setting: Yahwe)". Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb, so the deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns ("wangu", "yeye", "wake") and Swahili has fewer such spans than English.

decisions.choice: "mtumishi wa BWANA" for Moses at every level; "mhudumu" (L), "msaidizi" (B, R) for Joshua
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua, as in the Pentateuch and Psalms: "Moses the servant of the LORD" is a title of honor, so Swahili says "mtumishi" at every level rather than "mtumwa" (a slave). Joshua is called by a different word, an aide who waits on his master: "mhudumu" at Literal, "msaidizi" (assistant, helper) at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "siervo" for Moses at every level; "ayudante" for Joshua
alternatives: "esclavo" at Literal, as the English Literal "slave"
decisions.reason: The terms note for Joshua, Judges and Ruth keeps "siervo" for Moses' title "the servant of the LORD" at every level, as in Psalms, so the Spanish Literal says "siervo" where the English Literal says "slave". Joshua's title is a different Hebrew word for a personal aide, given as "ayudante", as in Deuteronomy 1:38.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("parla") and the passé composé at Readable ("a parlé"); speeches in the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua 1-12, as in the Pentateuch: the French style guide sets the passé simple, the tense of written narrative, at Literal and Balanced, and the passé composé, the tense French readers use and hear every day, at Readable. Speeches (God's charge to Joshua, the spies' report, Joshua's farewell words) keep the tenses of speech at every level.

decisions.choice: the divine name as "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals ("du SEIGNEUR", "au SEIGNEUR"), with "Yahvé" as the reader setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua 1-12, as in the Pentateuch: the name of God is "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", and the reader can choose "Yahvé". The setting takes in the article and its contraction ("du SEIGNEUR" or "de Yahvé"). "L'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the alternative a reviewer may prefer; plain "le Seigneur" would hide that the name is used. Moses is "serviteur du SEIGNEUR" at every level, Literal included, as the terms note sets for this title.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ" for Moses at every level; "người hầu cận" (L) / "người phụ tá" (B) / "người giúp việc cho Môi-se" (R) for Joshua
alternatives: "nô lệ" at Literal, as the English Literal "slave"
decisions.reason: The Genesis terms note renders the Hebrew word for slave or servant as "đầy tớ", keeping "nô lệ" for places where slavery itself is the point; as a title of honor ("the servant of the LORD", m2) "đầy tớ" is right at every level, and "nô lệ" would make Moses sound like a chattel slave. Joshua's title is a different Hebrew word (m3), so it gets a different Vietnamese word: an aide who serves a superior, not a slave.

decisions.choice: "Giô-suê con trai Nun"
decisions.reason: The form of the name given in the terms note for Joshua, Judges and Ruth; "con trai Nun" follows the way Genesis gives a father's name.

decisions.choice: "종" for Moses at every level; "시종" (L), "보좌하던" (B), "돕던 사람" (R) for Joshua
alternatives: "노예" for Moses at Literal, as the English Literal "slave"
decisions.reason: Korean "종" already covers both slave and servant, so it stands at every level for Moses, the servant of the LORD, as in Genesis; "노예" is kept for slavery itself. Joshua's title is a different word, for a personal aide, so Korean uses words for an assistant, not "종".

decisions.choice: o escravo do SENHOR (L), o servo do SENHOR (B, R) for Moses; o auxiliar (L, B), o ajudante (R) for Joshua
decisions.reason: For the whole book. The two Hebrew words differ, so Portuguese keeps them apart, as the English does. Moses' title takes the word for a slave (m2), "escravo" at Literal and "servo" at Balanced and Readable, as docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md sets it; Joshua's word names a personal aide (m3), "auxiliar" and "ajudante", the words Exodus 24:13 uses for him in Portuguese, never "servo".

decisions.choice: Josué, filho de Num
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the name and the father's name in the Brazilian forms Exodus 33:11 and Numbers 27:18 use in Portuguese, with "filho de Num" set off by commas as there.

es.L: «Moisés, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, ha muerto. Y ahora levántate, cruza este Jordán, tú y todo este pueblo, hacia la tierra que yo les doy a ellos, a los hijos de Israel.

vi.L: "Môi-se, đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã chết. Vậy bây giờ, hãy đứng dậy, đi qua sông Giô-đanh này, ngươi và cả dân này, vào xứ mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang ban cho họ, cho con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: "Môi-se, đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã qua đời. Bây giờ con hãy đứng dậy, cùng cả dân này đi qua sông Giô-đanh, vào xứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp ban cho họ, tức là cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: "Môi-se, đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã qua đời. Bây giờ con hãy sẵn sàng đi qua sông Giô-đanh, con và cả dân này. Hãy đi vào xứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang ban cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: "내 종 모세가 죽었다. 그러므로 이제 일어나, 너와 이 모든 백성은 이 요단을 건너, 내가 그들에게, 곧 이스라엘 자손에게 주는 땅으로 가거라.
ko.B: "내 종 모세가 죽었다. 이제 너는 이 모든 백성과 함께 일어나 이 요단강을 건너서, 내가 이스라엘 자손에게 주려는 땅으로 들어가거라.
ko.R: "내 종 모세가 죽었다. 이제 너는 이 모든 백성과 함께 요단강을 건널 준비를 하여라. 내가 이스라엘 백성에게 주는 땅으로 들어가거라.

pt.L: "Moisés, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} escravo, está morto. E agora levanta-te, atravessa este Jordão, tu e todo este povo, para a terra que eu dou a eles, aos filhos de Israel.
pt.B: "O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Moisés morreu. Agora levanta-te e atravessa este Jordão, tu e todo este povo, para entrar na terra que estou dando a eles, aos israelitas.
pt.R: "O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Moisés morreu. Agora prepara-te para atravessar o rio Jordão, tu e todo este povo. Vai para a terra que estou dando aos israelitas.

decisions.choice: arise: get up and act; a call to begin, not only to stand
decisions.reason: "Arise" often comes before another command and urges someone to start at once (Genesis 13:17; Deuteronomy 10:11). The time of mourning for Moses is over (Deuteronomy 34:8), and the LORD tells Joshua to set out.

decisions.choice: I am giving: a gift already under way and about to be completed
decisions.reason: The verb is a participle, which can describe something happening now or about to happen. God is in the act of giving the land; Israel has yet to cross over and take it.

decisions.choice: to them, to the sons of Israel: the second phrase names who "them" are
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to them" and then adds "to the sons of Israel" to make plain that the land is the gift of the whole people, not of Joshua alone.

decisions.choice: the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" so young readers know what the Jordan is, and splits the long command in two.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Israeli" (L); "Waisraeli" (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua, as in the Pentateuch: "wana" means children of either sex, so the Literal "wana wa Israeli" is already inclusive, and Balanced and Readable say "Waisraeli". Swahili has no second wording for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "serviteur" for Moses at every level, Literal included
alternatives: "esclave" at Literal, as for other uses of the word
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "slave" here to show the hard sense of the word. In French, as in Psalms and the Pentateuch, "Moïse, serviteur du SEIGNEUR" is kept at every level: it is a title of honour, and "esclave" would make it sound like a man bought and sold.

decisions.choice: les enfants d'Israël (Literal), les Israélites (Balanced, Readable), with "fils" as the gender setting
alternatives: les fils d'Israël with no setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua 1-12, as in the Pentateuch: the phrase means the whole people, women as well as men, so the default is inclusive, as in English; the reader can choose the traditional "fils d'Israël".

decisions.choice: God speaks to Joshua in the plain style (해라체) with "나" and "너"; no deity_pronoun spans in Korean
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for God speaking to people. Korean has no capital letters, so the English setting for capitalising pronouns for God has nothing to change here; respect for God is carried by the honorific endings in the narrative.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (L, B), "이스라엘 백성" (R), with no gender setting
alternatives: "이스라엘의 아들들", with "자손" as a setting alternative
decisions.reason: The Korean words "자손" (descendants) and "백성" (people) already include women and men, so Korean has no second form for the gender setting to switch to, as in Psalms.

decisions.choice: God calls Joshua "ngươi" (L), "con" (B, R) and himself "Ta"; his words to Israel as a nation are "các ngươi" at every level
decisions.reason: God speaking to one person who serves him calls him "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable, as the Genesis terms note and the Pentateuch set; God's words to a king or priest he is judging, to Israel as a nation, and to the nations keep "ngươi" / "các ngươi" at every level. "ngươi" keeps the plain form of the Hebrew at Literal; "con" gives the warmth of a father to a son at Balanced and Readable. Recorded once here for the book.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L), "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender setting to choose between "children" and "sons". Vietnamese "con cháu" already means all the descendants, sons and daughters, and "dân" means the whole people, so the Vietnamese has only one form and no setting; "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" is the Literal form of the Pentateuch. The same holds through the book.

decisions.choice: tu (the LORD to Joshua); vocês (Joshua and the LORD to the people in the plural); o senhor (the people to Joshua)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in the Pentateuch: God speaks to one man with "tu" ("levanta-te", "atravessa"), as he speaks to Moses. Where the Hebrew "you" turns plural (verses 3-4) Portuguese says "vocês", following the Hebrew number. Joshua speaks to the officials and the people with "vocês", and they answer their leader with "o senhor" (verses 16-18), as Reuben and Gad answer Moses in Numbers 32:25 in Portuguese. The spies and Rahab speak to each other with "você" (chapter 2).

decisions.choice: eu dou (L); estou dando (B, R); os filhos de Israel (L), os israelitas (B, R), no gender setting
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas de Israel
decisions.reason: For the whole book. The land formula keeps Deuteronomy's wording (Deuteronomy 1:20): the participle of a gift under way (m2) is the plain present "dou", "dá" at Literal and "estou dando", "está dando" at Balanced and Readable, "te dá" / "está te dando" with "tu". "Os filhos de Israel" (L) and "os israelitas" (B, R) take no setting, as in Genesis to Deuteronomy: "filhos" already includes daughters, so there is nothing for a setting to change.

records.literal_gloss: Every place which will tread [the] sole of your foot on it, to you I have given it, just as I spoke to Moses.

en.L: Every place on which the sole of your foot treads, I have given it to you, just as I spoke to Moses.
en.B: I have given you every place where you set foot, just as I promised Moses.
en.R: I have given you every place you walk on, just as I promised Moses.

sw.L: Kila mahali ambapo nyayo za miguu yenu zitakanyaga, nimewapa ninyi, kama nilivyomwambia Musa.
sw.B: Nimewapa kila mahali mtakapokanyaga kwa miguu yenu, kama nilivyomwahidi Musa.
sw.R: Nimewapa kila mahali mtakapotembea, kama nilivyomwahidi Musa.

es.L: Todo lugar que pise la planta {{plural_you:del pie de ustedes|de vuestro pie}}, {{plural_you:a ustedes se lo|a vosotros os lo}} he dado, tal como dije a Moisés.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dado todo lugar donde {{plural_you:pongan|pongáis}} el pie, tal como se lo prometí a Moisés.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dado todo lugar por donde {{plural_you:caminen|caminéis}}, tal como se lo prometí a Moisés.

fr.L: Tout lieu que foulera la plante de votre pied, je vous l’ai donné, comme je l’ai dit à Moïse.
fr.B: Je vous ai donné tout lieu où vous poserez le pied, comme je l’ai promis à Moïse.
fr.R: Je vous ai donné tous les endroits où vous marcherez, comme je l’ai promis à Moïse.

vi.L: Mọi nơi bàn chân các ngươi giẫm lên, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban nơi ấy cho các ngươi, đúng như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phán với Môi-se.
vi.B: Ta đã ban cho các con mọi nơi các con đặt chân đến, đúng như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã hứa với Môi-se.
vi.R: Ta đã ban cho các con mọi nơi các con bước chân đến, đúng như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã hứa với Môi-se.

ko.L: 너희 발바닥이 밟는 모든 곳을, 내가 모세에게 말한 그대로 너희에게 주었다.
ko.B: 내가 모세에게 약속한 대로, 너희가 발을 딛는 곳마다 내가 너희에게 주었다.
ko.R: 내가 모세에게 약속한 대로, 너희가 걸어가는 곳은 어디든지 내가 너희에게 주었다.

pt.L: Todo lugar em que pisar a planta do pé de vocês, eu o dei a vocês, como falei a Moisés.
pt.B: Eu dei a vocês todo lugar em que puserem o pé, como prometi a Moisés.
pt.R: Eu dei a vocês todo lugar onde vocês pisarem, como prometi a Moisés.

decisions.choice: every place the sole of your foot treads: every place you go into and claim
decisions.reason: To set foot on land is to enter it and take hold of it. God had made this promise to Israel through Moses in the same words (Deuteronomy 11:24).

decisions.choice: your, you: plural; the promise is to all the people
decisions.reason: In verse 2 God speaks to Joshua alone, but here "your" and "you" are plural. The promise belongs to the whole people whom Joshua leads. In verse 5 the address turns back to Joshua.

decisions.choice: I have given it: a promise spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for completed action, though the land is not yet won. God speaks of it as settled because he has decided it.

decisions.choice: just as I spoke to Moses: the promise of Deuteronomy 11:24-25
decisions.reason: The verb "spoke" here means "promised". God refers back to what he had said through Moses (Deuteronomy 11:24-25), and verses 3-5 repeat that promise almost word for word.

decisions.choice: I have given you every place ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "I have given you" first, as English does, instead of naming the place and then picking it up again with "it".

decisions.choice: plural "-enu", "ninyi", "mtakapo-"
alternatives: singular "wako", "wewe", following Joshua as the one addressed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from Joshua ("you" singular, verse 2) to the people ("you" plural) here. Swahili marks the difference in every verb and pronoun, so the plural is kept, and the promise is heard as made to all Israel.

decisions.choice: plural "you" (ustedes / vosotros) in verses 3-4
decisions.reason: God speaks to Joshua with "tú", but here "your" and "you" are plural in the Hebrew: the promise is to all the people. Spanish can show this, so these two verses switch to the plural forms and go back to "tú" in verse 5.

decisions.choice: "vous" (plural) in this verse, though God is speaking to Joshua
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" and "you" are plural here: the promise is to the whole people. French can show this, so it switches from "tu" (to Joshua) to "vous" (to all of them), where English "you" cannot.

decisions.choice: "các ngươi" (L), "các con" (B, R): plural
decisions.reason: In this verse the Hebrew "you" is plural (m2): the promise is to the whole people, not to Joshua alone. Vietnamese marks the plural, which the English "you" cannot show.

decisions.choice: the plural "너희" here, though God has been speaking to Joshua as "너"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" and "you" in this verse are plural: the promise is to all the people. Korean can show the plural, so it does.

decisions.choice: vocês (verses 3-4)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from Joshua to the whole people here (m2), so Portuguese turns from "tu" to "vocês" for these two verses and back to "tu" in verse 5, following the Hebrew number as Deuteronomy does (Deuteronomy 11:24 has the same promise in Portuguese).

source.text: מֵהַמִּדְבָּר֩ וְהַלְּבָנ֨וֹן הַזֶּ֜ה וְֽעַד־הַנָּהָ֧ר הַגָּד֣וֹל נְהַר־פְּרָ֗ת כֹּ֚ל אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽחִתִּ֔ים וְעַד־הַיָּ֥ם הַגָּד֖וֹל מְב֣וֹא הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ יִֽהְיֶ֖ה גְּבוּלְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: From the wilderness and the Lebanon the this and to the river the great, [the] river Euphrates, all [the] land of the Hittites, and to the sea the great, [the] setting of the sun, will be your territory.

en.L: From the wilderness and this Lebanon, and as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun, will be your territory.
en.B: Your territory will reach from the wilderness to this Lebanon, and as far as the great river, the Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and west to the Great Sea where the sun sets.
en.R: Your land will reach from the desert in the south to the Lebanon mountains in the north. It will reach east to the great Euphrates River, taking in all the land of the Hittites. And it will reach west to the Mediterranean Sea.

sw.L: Kutoka nyika na Lebanoni hii, hadi mto mkubwa, mto Frati, nchi yote ya Wahiti, hadi Bahari Kuu upande wa machweo ya jua, itakuwa mipaka yenu.
sw.B: Nchi yenu itaanzia nyikani hadi Lebanoni hii, na hadi mto mkubwa, Frati, nchi yote ya Wahiti, na upande wa magharibi hadi Bahari Kuu, jua linapotua.
sw.R: Nchi yenu itaenea kutoka jangwa la kusini hadi milima ya Lebanoni upande wa kaskazini. Itafika upande wa mashariki hadi mto mkubwa wa Frati, ikijumuisha nchi yote ya Wahiti. Na upande wa magharibi itafika hadi Bahari ya Mediterania.

es.L: Desde el desierto y este Líbano hasta el gran río, el río Éufrates, toda la tierra de los hititas, y hasta el mar Grande, hacia la puesta del sol, será {{plural_you:su territorio|vuestro territorio}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Su territorio|Vuestro territorio}} irá desde el desierto hasta este Líbano, y hasta el gran río, el Éufrates, toda la tierra de los hititas, y al oeste hasta el mar Grande, donde se pone el sol.
es.R: {{plural_you:Su tierra|Vuestra tierra}} irá desde el desierto, en el sur, hasta los montes del Líbano, en el norte. Llegará al este hasta el gran río Éufrates, con toda la tierra de los hititas. Y llegará al oeste hasta el mar Mediterráneo.

fr.L: Depuis le désert et ce Liban jusqu’au grand fleuve, le fleuve Euphrate, tout le pays des Hittites, et jusqu’à la Grande Mer, vers le coucher du soleil, ce sera votre territoire.
fr.B: Votre territoire s’étendra du désert jusqu’à ce Liban, et jusqu’au grand fleuve, l’Euphrate, tout le pays des Hittites, et à l’ouest jusqu’à la Grande Mer, là où le soleil se couche.
fr.R: Votre pays ira du désert, au sud, jusqu’aux montagnes du Liban, au nord. À l’est, il ira jusqu’au grand fleuve Euphrate et comprendra tout le pays des Hittites. À l’ouest, il ira jusqu’à la mer Méditerranée.

vi.L: Từ hoang mạc và Li-ban này cho đến sông lớn, sông Ơ-phơ-rát, toàn xứ của người Hê-tít, và cho đến Biển Lớn phía mặt trời lặn, sẽ là bờ cõi của các ngươi.
vi.B: Bờ cõi các con sẽ trải từ hoang mạc đến Li-ban này, đến tận sông lớn là sông Ơ-phơ-rát, gồm toàn xứ của người Hê-tít, và về phía tây đến tận Biển Lớn, nơi mặt trời lặn.
vi.R: Đất của các con sẽ trải dài từ hoang mạc ở phía nam đến dãy núi Li-ban ở phía bắc. Về phía đông, đất ấy sẽ đến tận sông lớn Ơ-phơ-rát, gồm toàn xứ của người Hê-tít. Về phía tây, đất ấy sẽ đến tận biển Địa Trung Hải.

ko.L: 광야와 이 레바논에서부터 큰 강, 곧 유프라테스강까지, 헷 사람들의 온 땅과 해 지는 쪽의 대해까지가 너희 영토가 될 것이다.
ko.B: 너희 영토는 광야에서 이 레바논까지, 그리고 큰 강 유프라테스까지 헷 사람들의 온 땅에 이르고, 서쪽으로는 해 지는 쪽의 대해까지 이를 것이다.
ko.R: 너희 땅은 남쪽의 광야에서 북쪽의 레바논 산지까지 이를 것이다. 동쪽으로는 큰 강 유프라테스까지 이르러, 헷 사람들의 온 땅이 들어갈 것이다. 서쪽으로는 지중해까지 이를 것이다.

pt.L: Desde o deserto e este Líbano até o grande rio, o rio Eufrates, toda a terra dos hititas, e até o Grande Mar, do lado do pôr do sol, será o território de vocês.
pt.B: O território de vocês irá do deserto até este Líbano, e até o grande rio, o Eufrates, toda a terra dos hititas, e a oeste até o Grande Mar, onde o sol se põe.
pt.R: A terra de vocês vai do deserto, no sul, até as montanhas do Líbano, no norte. Vai a leste até o grande rio Eufrates e inclui toda a terra dos hititas. E vai a oeste até o mar Mediterrâneo.

decisions.choice: the borders: the southern wilderness, Lebanon in the north, the Euphrates in the north-east, the Mediterranean in the west
decisions.reason: The wilderness is the dry land to the south, toward Sinai. Lebanon is the mountain range to the north. "The great river" is the Euphrates, far to the north-east. "The Great Sea toward the setting of the sun" is the Mediterranean, on the west. These are the widest limits of the promise, as in Genesis 15:18 and Deuteronomy 11:24.

decisions.choice: this Lebanon: Lebanon pointed to as if in sight
decisions.reason: The word "this" points to Lebanon as though God were showing Joshua the land laid out before him, as he had shown it to Moses from Mount Nebo (Deuteronomy 34:1-4).

decisions.choice: all the land of the Hittites: here the lands of Syria toward the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The Hittites were a people whose empire lay to the north, in what is now Turkey, and whose name was later used for the peoples and kingdoms of Syria. The phrase names the northern part of the promised territory between Lebanon and the Euphrates.

decisions.choice: all the land of the Hittites: kept, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: leave out "all the land of the Hittites"
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation does not have the words "all the land of the Hittites", and the parallel promise in Deuteronomy 11:24 does not have them either. They may have been added to the Hebrew as an explanation, or the Greek may have left them out. The Hebrew text is followed here. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek translation and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: in the south ... in the north ... east ... west; the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable adds the directions and the modern name of the sea, following the meaning decisions, and breaks the long list into short sentences.

decisions.choice: "nyika" (nyikani) at Literal and Balanced, "jangwa" at Readable
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua, as in Deuteronomy: the midbar is open, dry grazing land rather than sand desert, which "nyika" says; Readable uses "jangwa", the everyday word.

decisions.choice: o Grande Mar (L, B); o mar Mediterrâneo (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as Numbers 34:6 has it in Portuguese: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew name with both words capitalised, as a name; Readable gives the modern name (m1), as the English does.

source.text: לֹֽא־יִתְיַצֵּ֥ב אִישׁ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּ֑יךָ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיִ֤יתִי עִם־מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א אַרְפְּךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א אֶעֶזְבֶֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will stand a man before you all [the] days of your life; just as I was with Moses, I will be with you; not I will let you drop and not I will leave you.

en.L: {{gender:No one|No man}} will stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I was with Moses, I will be with you; I will not let you go, and I will not abandon you.
en.B: {{gender:No one|No man}} will be able to stand against you as long as you live. I will be with you just as I was with Moses. I will not let go of you or abandon you.
en.R: As long as you live, {{gender:no one|no man}} will be able to stand up to you. I will be with you just as I was with Moses. I will never let you go, and I will never leave you alone.

sw.L: Hakuna mtu atakayesimama mbele yako siku zote za maisha yako. Kama nilivyokuwa pamoja na Musa, nitakuwa pamoja nawe; sitakuacha, wala sitakutupa.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu atakayeweza kusimama dhidi yako maadamu unaishi. Nitakuwa pamoja nawe kama nilivyokuwa pamoja na Musa. Sitakuachilia wala sitakutupa.
sw.R: Maisha yako yote, hakuna mtu atakayeweza kukushinda. Nitakuwa pamoja nawe kama nilivyokuwa pamoja na Musa. Sitakuacha kamwe, wala sitakuacha peke yako.

es.L: {{gender:Nadie|Ningún hombre}} se mantendrá en pie delante de ti todos los días de tu vida. Como estuve con Moisés, estaré contigo; no te soltaré, y no te abandonaré.
es.B: {{gender:Nadie|Ningún hombre}} podrá hacerte frente mientras vivas. Estaré contigo así como estuve con Moisés. No te soltaré ni te abandonaré.
es.R: Mientras vivas, {{gender:nadie|ningún hombre}} podrá hacerte frente. Estaré contigo como estuve con Moisés. Nunca te soltaré y nunca te dejaré solo.

fr.L: Personne ne tiendra devant toi tous les jours de ta vie. Comme j’ai été avec Moïse, je serai avec toi ; je ne te lâcherai pas et je ne t’abandonnerai pas.
fr.B: Personne ne pourra te résister tant que tu vivras. Je serai avec toi comme j’ai été avec Moïse. Je ne te lâcherai pas et je ne t’abandonnerai pas.
fr.R: Aussi longtemps que tu vivras, personne ne pourra te résister. Je serai avec toi comme j’ai été avec Moïse. Je ne te lâcherai jamais et je ne te laisserai jamais seul.

vi.L: Sẽ không ai đứng nổi trước mặt ngươi trọn mọi ngày của đời ngươi. Ta đã ở với Môi-se thể nào, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ở với ngươi thể ấy; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không buông ngươi ra, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không bỏ ngươi.
vi.B: Trọn đời con, sẽ không ai chống cự nổi con. Ta sẽ ở với con như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ở với Môi-se. Ta sẽ không buông con ra, cũng không bỏ con.
vi.R: Suốt đời con, sẽ không ai đứng lên chống lại con được. Ta sẽ ở với con như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ở với Môi-se. Ta sẽ không bao giờ buông con ra, và không bao giờ để con một mình.

ko.L: 네 평생에 아무도 네 앞에 맞서지 못할 것이다. 내가 모세와 함께 있었던 것처럼 너와 함께 있겠다. 내가 너를 놓지 않고, 너를 버리지 않겠다.
ko.B: 네가 사는 동안 아무도 너를 당해 내지 못할 것이다. 내가 모세와 함께 있었던 것처럼 너와도 함께 있겠다. 나는 너를 놓지 않고 버리지도 않겠다.
ko.R: 네가 살아 있는 동안 아무도 너를 이기지 못할 것이다. 내가 모세와 함께 있었던 것처럼 너와도 함께 있겠다. 나는 절대로 너를 놓지 않고, 너를 혼자 내버려 두지 않겠다.

pt.L: Ninguém resistirá diante de ti todos os dias da tua vida. Como estive com Moisés, estarei contigo; não te largarei e não te abandonarei.
pt.B: Ninguém conseguirá te enfrentar enquanto viveres. Estarei contigo como estive com Moisés. Não te largarei nem te abandonarei.
pt.R: Enquanto viveres, ninguém vai conseguir te enfrentar. Eu vou estar contigo, como estive com Moisés. Nunca vou te largar e nunca vou te deixar sozinho.

decisions.choice: stand before you: hold out against you
decisions.reason: To "stand before" an enemy is to resist him and hold one's ground (Deuteronomy 7:24; 11:25). The word is "man", but the sense is "no one at all".

decisions.choice: I will be with you: God's promised presence, as with Moses
decisions.reason: "I will be with you" is the promise God made to Moses when he sent him (Exodus 3:12). Joshua is promised the same help Moses had, and the people pray for it in verse 17. The promise is the ground for the command in verses 6-9.

decisions.choice: I will not let you go, and I will not abandon you: God will neither loosen his hold nor leave
decisions.reason: The first verb means to let something drop or to loosen one's grip; the second means to leave or abandon. Moses had said the same of God to the people and to Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:6, 8).

decisions.choice: No one / No man
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a man" in the sense of "anyone". The default reads "no one"; the traditional setting keeps "no man", as in Deuteronomy 11:25.

decisions.choice: "mtu" (a person), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili "mtu" already means any person, man or woman, so there is no second wording for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: "personne" with no gender setting, where the English has one (No one / No man)
decisions.reason: French "personne" already means anyone, man or woman, so it needs no setting; the French style guide keeps generic words such as "personne", "quiconque" and "chacun" without one.

decisions.choice: "không ai" with no gender span
alternatives: a span between "không ai" and "không người đàn ông nào"
decisions.reason: The English offers "No one" or "No man". Vietnamese "không ai" is the ordinary way to say it and already covers men and women, so there is nothing for a setting to switch; the same holds for "bất cứ ai" (anyone) in this book.

decisions.choice: "아무도" with no gender setting
alternatives: a span such as "어떤 남자도" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a man", meaning anyone at all. Korean "아무도" (no one) is already the inclusive word and has no traditional masculine form beside it, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: Ninguém, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting because "no man" names only men, while the sense is "no one at all" (m1). Portuguese "ninguém" already says that, as Deuteronomy 11:25 has it in Portuguese, so there is nothing for a setting to change.

decisions.choice: não te largarei (L, B), nunca vou te largar (R)
decisions.reason: The first verb means to loosen one's grip (m3); "largar" says that in everyday Portuguese and keeps it apart from "abandonar" for the second verb.

source.text: חֲזַ֖ק וֶאֱמָ֑ץ כִּ֣י אַתָּ֗ה תַּנְחִיל֙ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶת־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Be strong and be bold, for you will cause to inherit the people the this the land which I swore to their fathers to give to them.

en.L: Be strong and bold, for you will cause this people to inherit the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.
en.B: Be strong and courageous, because you are the one who will lead this people to take as their inheritance the land I swore to their ancestors to give them.
en.R: Be strong and brave. You are the one who will lead these people to take the land as their own. It is the land I promised with an oath to give their ancestors.

sw.L: Uwe imara na jasiri, kwa maana wewe utawarithisha watu hawa nchi ambayo niliwaapia baba zao kuwapa.
sw.B: Uwe imara na jasiri, kwa sababu wewe ndiwe utakayewaongoza watu hawa kuirithi nchi niliyowaapia babu zao kuwapa.
sw.R: Uwe imara na shujaa. Wewe ndiwe utakayewaongoza watu hawa kuichukua nchi iwe yao. Ni nchi ile niliyowaahidi babu zao kwa kiapo kwamba nitawapa.

es.L: Sé fuerte y valeroso, porque tú harás que este pueblo herede la tierra que juré a sus padres que les daría.
es.B: Sé fuerte y valiente, porque tú eres quien guiará a este pueblo a recibir como herencia la tierra que juré a sus antepasados que les daría.
es.R: Sé fuerte y valiente. Tú eres quien guiará a este pueblo para que tome la tierra como suya. Es la tierra que prometí con juramento dar a sus antepasados.

fr.L: Sois fort et courageux, car c’est toi qui feras hériter ce peuple du pays que j’ai juré à leurs pères de leur donner.
fr.B: Sois fort et courageux, car c’est toi qui conduiras ce peuple à recevoir en héritage le pays que j’ai juré à leurs ancêtres de leur donner.
fr.R: Sois fort et courageux. C’est toi qui vas conduire ce peuple pour qu’il prenne ce pays et le garde pour lui. C’est le pays que j’ai promis par serment de donner à leurs ancêtres.

vi.L: Hãy mạnh mẽ và dạn dĩ, vì chính ngươi sẽ làm cho dân này nhận được xứ mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thề với tổ phụ họ là sẽ ban cho họ làm sản nghiệp.
vi.B: Hãy mạnh mẽ và can đảm, vì chính con sẽ dẫn dân này nhận lấy làm sản nghiệp xứ mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thề với tổ tiên họ là sẽ ban cho họ.
vi.R: Hãy mạnh mẽ và dũng cảm. Chính con sẽ dẫn dân này chiếm lấy xứ làm của mình. Đó là xứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thề hứa ban cho tổ tiên họ.

ko.L: 강하고 담대하여라. 네가 이 백성에게, 내가 그들의 조상들에게 주겠다고 맹세한 땅을 유산으로 차지하게 할 것이다.
ko.B: 강하고 담대하여라. 내가 이 백성의 조상들에게 주겠다고 맹세한 땅을 이 백성이 유산으로 차지하도록 이끌 사람이 바로 너다.
ko.R: 힘을 내고 용기를 가져라. 이 백성을 이끌어 그 땅을 자기 땅으로 차지하게 할 사람은 바로 너다. 그 땅은 내가 그들의 조상들에게 주겠다고 맹세하며 약속한 땅이다.

pt.L: Sê forte e corajoso, pois tu farás este povo herdar a terra que jurei aos pais deles que lhes daria.
pt.B: Sê forte e corajoso, porque és tu quem fará este povo receber como herança a terra que jurei aos antepassados deles que lhes daria.
pt.R: Sê forte e corajoso. És tu quem vai levar este povo a tomar posse da terra. É a terra que prometi com juramento dar aos antepassados deles.

decisions.choice: be strong and be bold: stand firm and do not lose heart
decisions.reason: The two verbs say nearly the same thing: be firm, be steady, take courage. Moses gave Joshua this charge in front of all Israel (Deuteronomy 31:7, 23), and God now repeats it three times (verses 6, 7, 9). The people say it to Joshua again at the end of the chapter (verse 18).

decisions.choice: you will cause this people to inherit: Joshua is the one who will lead them into their inheritance
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is stressed. Moses could not bring the people in (Deuteronomy 31:2); Joshua will. The verb means to give someone land as an inheritance, a lasting family share, which Joshua does when he divides the land (chapters 13-21).

decisions.choice: the land I swore to their fathers: the oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God promised the land with an oath to Israel's ancestors (Genesis 26:3; 50:24; Deuteronomy 1:8; 34:4).

decisions.choice: be bold (Literal) / courageous (Balanced) / brave (Readable)
decisions.reason: The second verb means to be firm and bold. Literal keeps two separate commands; Balanced joins them; Readable uses the common word "brave". The same words are used in verses 7, 9 and 18.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the forefathers of the people, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

decisions.choice: "imara na jasiri" (L, B); "imara na shujaa" (R)
decisions.reason: For this book, which repeats the charge (verses 7, 9, 18; 10:25): "imara" says standing firm, "jasiri" bold and unafraid; Readable uses "shujaa", the everyday word for a brave person. The pair is kept the same each time so that the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: "sé fuerte y valeroso" (Literal); "sé fuerte y valiente" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The second verb means to be firm and bold. Literal uses the less common "valeroso" to keep it apart from everyday "valiente"; Balanced and Readable use "valiente", the plain word. The same words return in verses 7, 9 and 18 and later in the book.

decisions.choice: "fort et courageux" at every level, for the charge repeated in verses 6, 7, 9 and 18
decisions.reason: The English uses three words by level (bold, courageous, brave). In French "courageux" is both the exact and the plain word, so the same phrase is kept at every level and the repeated charge sounds the same each time.

decisions.choice: "mạnh mẽ và dạn dĩ" (L) / "mạnh mẽ và can đảm" (B) / "mạnh mẽ và dũng cảm" (R)
decisions.reason: The charge comes back through the chapter (verses 7, 9, 18). Each level keeps one wording each time: "dạn dĩ" (bold) at Literal, "can đảm" (courageous) at Balanced, the everyday "dũng cảm" (brave) at Readable.

decisions.choice: "nhận ... làm sản nghiệp"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is the one for receiving an inheritance. "sản nghiệp" is the word the terms note sets for inheritance in these books, and Acts 13:19 already uses it for this same gift of the land.

decisions.choice: "강하고 담대하여라" (L, B); "힘을 내고 용기를 가져라" (R), the same at each repetition of the charge
decisions.reason: The charge comes back in verses 7, 9 and 18 and later in the book, so each level keeps one wording for it. "담대하다" is the word for boldness of heart; Readable uses everyday words for the same two commands.

decisions.choice: Sê forte e corajoso (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (verses 6, 7, 9, 18; 10:25): the charge given to Joshua in Deuteronomy 31, where God says "Sê forte e corajoso" (31:23), Moses "Seja forte e corajoso" (31:7) and the people are told "Sejam fortes e corajosos" (31:6). The two verbs say nearly the same thing (m1); "corajoso" is plain enough for every level, where the English moves from "bold" to "courageous" and "brave". God says it to Joshua with "tu", "Sê"; the people say it with "o senhor", "Seja" (verse 18).

source.text: רַק֩ חֲזַ֨ק וֶֽאֱמַ֜ץ מְאֹ֗ד לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ כְּכָל־הַתּוֹרָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוְּךָ֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדִּ֔י אַל־תָּס֥וּר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֔יל בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Only be strong and be bold very, to take care to do according to all the law which commanded you Moses my servant; do not turn from it right and left, so that you may act wisely in all that you will go.

en.L: Only be strong and very bold, to take care to do according to all the law that Moses {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave commanded you. Do not turn aside from it [to the] right or [to the] left, so that you may act wisely and succeed wherever you go.
en.B: Only be strong and very courageous. Take care to keep the whole law that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses laid on you. Do not swerve from it to right or left, and then you will act wisely and succeed wherever you go.
en.R: Above all, be strong and very brave. Be careful to obey all the teaching that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses gave you. Do not wander away from it in any direction. Then you will act wisely and do well wherever you go.

sw.L: Ila tu uwe imara na jasiri sana, ili uangalie kutenda sawasawa na sheria yote ambayo Musa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} alikuamuru. Usiiache kwenda kulia wala kushoto, ili utende kwa hekima na kufanikiwa kila mahali utakapokwenda.
sw.B: Ila tu uwe imara na jasiri sana. Uwe mwangalifu kuishika sheria yote ambayo mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Musa alikuagiza. Usigeuke kutoka kwake kwenda kulia wala kushoto, nawe utatenda kwa hekima na kufanikiwa kila mahali utakapokwenda.
sw.R: Zaidi ya yote, uwe imara na shujaa sana. Uwe mwangalifu kutii mafundisho yote ambayo mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Musa alikupa. Usiyaache hata kidogo. Ndipo utakapotenda kwa hekima na kufanikiwa kila mahali utakapokwenda.

es.L: Solo sé fuerte y muy valeroso, para tener cuidado de obrar según toda la ley que te ordenó Moisés, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo. No te apartes de ella [a la] derecha ni [a la] izquierda, para que actúes con sabiduría y tengas éxito dondequiera que vayas.
es.B: Solo sé fuerte y muy valiente. Cuida de cumplir toda la ley que te encomendó {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Moisés. No te desvíes de ella ni a la derecha ni a la izquierda, y así actuarás con sabiduría y tendrás éxito dondequiera que vayas.
es.R: Sobre todo, sé fuerte y muy valiente. Ten cuidado de obedecer toda la enseñanza que te dio {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Moisés. No te alejes de ella en ninguna dirección. Así actuarás con sabiduría y te irá bien dondequiera que vayas.

fr.L: Seulement, sois fort et très courageux, pour veiller à agir selon toute la loi que t’a prescrite Moïse, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur. Ne t’en détourne ni [à] droite ni [à] gauche, afin que tu agisses avec sagesse et réussisses partout où tu iras.
fr.B: Seulement, sois fort et très courageux. Veille à observer toute la loi que t’a imposée Moïse, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur. Ne t’en écarte ni à droite ni à gauche, et tu agiras avec sagesse et réussiras partout où tu iras.
fr.R: Surtout, sois fort et très courageux. Fais bien attention à obéir à tout l’enseignement que Moïse, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, t’a donné. Ne t’en éloigne d’aucun côté. Alors tu agiras avec sagesse et tout ira bien pour toi partout où tu iras.

vi.L: Chỉ hãy mạnh mẽ và rất dạn dĩ, để cẩn thận làm theo mọi luật pháp mà Môi-se, đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã truyền cho ngươi. Chớ xây khỏi luật pháp ấy [mà qua] bên phải hay [qua] bên trái, để ngươi hành động khôn ngoan và thành công bất cứ nơi nào ngươi đi.
vi.B: Chỉ cần con mạnh mẽ và hết sức can đảm. Hãy cẩn thận giữ trọn luật pháp mà Môi-se, đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã truyền cho con. Đừng lệch khỏi luật pháp ấy, dù sang phải hay sang trái; như vậy con sẽ hành động khôn ngoan và thành công bất cứ nơi nào con đi.
vi.R: Trên hết mọi điều, con hãy mạnh mẽ và thật dũng cảm. Hãy cẩn thận vâng giữ tất cả lời dạy mà Môi-se, đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã truyền cho con. Đừng đi lệch khỏi lời dạy ấy chút nào. Như vậy con sẽ hành động khôn ngoan và làm việc gì cũng tốt đẹp, dù con đi đâu.

ko.L: 오직 강하고 매우 담대하여, 내 종 모세가 너에게 명령한 모든 율법을 따라 지켜 행하여라. 그것에서 떠나 오른쪽으로나 왼쪽으로나 치우치지 마라. 그러면 네가 어디로 가든지 지혜롭게 행하여 형통할 것이다.
ko.B: 오직 강하고 매우 담대하여라. 내 종 모세가 너에게 명령한 모든 율법을 지켜 행하도록 조심하여라. 그 율법에서 벗어나 오른쪽으로도 왼쪽으로도 치우치지 마라. 그러면 네가 어디로 가든지 지혜롭게 행하고 잘될 것이다.
ko.R: 무엇보다도 힘을 내고 아주 큰 용기를 가져라. 내 종 모세가 너에게 준 가르침을 모두 조심해서 지켜라. 그 가르침에서 조금도 벗어나지 마라. 그러면 네가 어디로 가든지 지혜롭게 행하고 하는 일이 잘될 것이다.

pt.L: Somente sê forte e muito corajoso, para cuidares de fazer conforme toda a lei que Moisés, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} escravo, te ordenou. Não te desvies dela [nem para a] direita nem [para a] esquerda, para que ajas sabiamente e tenhas êxito aonde quer que fores.
pt.B: Somente sê forte e muito corajoso. Cuida de cumprir toda a lei que o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Moisés te deu. Não te desvies dela nem para a direita nem para a esquerda, e então agirás com sabedoria e serás bem-sucedido aonde quer que fores.
pt.R: Acima de tudo, sê forte e muito corajoso. Tem o cuidado de obedecer a todo o ensino que o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Moisés te deu. Não te afastes dele em nenhuma direção. Assim vais agir com sabedoria e tudo vai dar certo aonde quer que fores.

decisions.choice: only be strong ... to take care to do: the courage God asks for here is courage to obey
decisions.reason: "Only" narrows the charge of verse 6. The strength Joshua needs is not only for battle but for keeping the whole law faithfully. The verb "take care" means to watch over, to keep carefully.

decisions.choice: the law: the instruction Moses gave, the whole of his teaching
decisions.reason: The word means instruction or teaching. As in Deuteronomy 1:5 and 31:9, "the law" is all that Moses taught Israel in God's name: the story of what God had done, the call to love him, and his commands.

decisions.choice: do not turn from it right or left: do not depart from it in any way
decisions.reason: The picture is of a road that must be kept without straying to either side (Deuteronomy 5:32; 17:11, 20; 28:14).

decisions.choice: act wisely: act with good sense, and so succeed
decisions.reason: The verb means to have insight and act with understanding, and so to do well and prosper. Moses promised that keeping the covenant would bring this kind of success (Deuteronomy 29:8).

decisions.choice: act wisely and succeed
decisions.reason: One Hebrew verb holds both acting wisely and its result, success. Literal and Balanced use two words to give both parts; Readable says "act wisely and do well".

decisions.choice: teaching; in any direction
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for "law", as in Deuteronomy 1:5, because "law" alone makes readers think only of rules. It also explains "right or left" as "in any direction".

decisions.choice: "sheria" (L, B); "mafundisho" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy: "sheria" follows the English "law" at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says "mafundisho" (teaching), as the English Readable does. "Torati" is familiar as the name of the five books, but here torah is the whole of what Moses taught.

decisions.choice: "luật pháp" (L, B), "lời dạy" (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, the word means Moses' whole instruction (m2). Literal and Balanced keep the familiar "luật pháp"; Readable says "lời dạy" (teaching), which does not narrow it to rules.

decisions.choice: a lei (L, B); o ensino (R)
decisions.reason: As Deuteronomy 1:5 sets it in Portuguese: the torah is the whole of Moses' teaching (m2), "lei" at Literal and Balanced and "ensino" at Readable, as the English Readable says "teaching"; the same in verse 8.

source.text: לֹֽא־יָמ֡וּשׁ סֵפֶר֩ הַתּוֹרָ֨ה הַזֶּ֜ה מִפִּ֗יךָ וְהָגִ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּכָל־הַכָּת֖וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּי־אָ֛ז תַּצְלִ֥יחַ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֖ךָ וְאָ֥ז תַּשְׂכִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will depart [the] book of the law the this from your mouth, and you will meditate on it by day and night, so that you may take care to do according to all the written in it; for then you will make prosper your ways, and then you will act wisely.

en.L: This book of the law will not depart from your mouth, and you will meditate on it day and night, so that you may take care to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your ways prosper, and then you will act wisely and succeed.
en.B: Keep this book of the law always on your lips, and reflect on it by day and by night, so that you take care to do all that is written in it. Then you will bring your ways to a good end, and then you will act wisely and succeed.
en.R: Always keep talking about the teaching in this book. Think about it during the day and at night. Then you will be careful to do everything written in it. If you do this, the things you do will go well, and you will act wisely and do well.

sw.L: Kitabu hiki cha sheria hakitaondoka kinywani mwako, nawe utakitafakari mchana na usiku, ili uangalie kutenda sawasawa na yote yaliyoandikwa ndani yake. Kwa maana hapo utazifanikisha njia zako, na hapo utatenda kwa hekima na kufanikiwa.
sw.B: Kitabu hiki cha sheria kiwe midomoni mwako daima, ukikitafakari mchana na usiku, ili uwe mwangalifu kufanya yote yaliyoandikwa ndani yake. Hapo njia zako zitafika mwisho mwema, nawe utatenda kwa hekima na kufanikiwa.
sw.R: Endelea kuyazungumza daima mafundisho yaliyo katika kitabu hiki. Yafikirie mchana na usiku. Ndipo utakapokuwa mwangalifu kufanya kila kitu kilichoandikwa ndani yake. Ukifanya hivyo, mambo yako yatakwenda vizuri, nawe utatenda kwa hekima na kufanikiwa.

es.L: Este libro de la ley no se apartará de tu boca, y meditarás en él de día y de noche, para que tengas cuidado de obrar según todo lo que está escrito en él. Porque entonces harás prosperar tus caminos, y entonces actuarás con sabiduría y tendrás éxito.
es.B: Ten siempre en tus labios este libro de la ley, y reflexiona en él de día y de noche, para que cuides de hacer todo lo que está escrito en él. Entonces llevarás a buen término tus caminos, y entonces actuarás con sabiduría y tendrás éxito.
es.R: Habla siempre de la enseñanza de este libro. Piensa en ella durante el día y por la noche. Así tendrás cuidado de hacer todo lo que está escrito en él. Si haces esto, te irá bien en lo que hagas, y actuarás con sabiduría y tendrás éxito.

fr.L: Ce livre de la loi ne s’éloignera pas de ta bouche, et tu le méditeras jour et nuit, afin que tu veilles à agir selon tout ce qui y est écrit. Car alors tu feras prospérer tes chemins, et alors tu agiras avec sagesse et réussiras.
fr.B: Garde toujours ce livre de la loi sur tes lèvres, et médite-le jour et nuit, afin de veiller à faire tout ce qui y est écrit. Alors tu mèneras tes entreprises à bonne fin, et alors tu agiras avec sagesse et réussiras.
fr.R: Parle sans cesse de l’enseignement de ce livre. Réfléchis-y le jour et la nuit. Ainsi tu feras attention à faire tout ce qui y est écrit. Si tu fais cela, ce que tu entreprendras réussira, et tu agiras avec sagesse et tout ira bien pour toi.

vi.L: Sách luật pháp này sẽ không lìa khỏi miệng ngươi, và ngươi sẽ suy ngẫm sách ấy ngày và đêm, để ngươi cẩn thận làm theo mọi điều đã chép trong đó. Vì khi ấy ngươi sẽ làm cho đường lối mình được thịnh vượng, và khi ấy ngươi sẽ hành động khôn ngoan và thành công.
vi.B: Hãy luôn luôn nói ra những lời của sách luật pháp này, và suy ngẫm sách ấy ngày đêm, để con cẩn thận làm theo mọi điều đã chép trong đó. Khi ấy đường lối con sẽ được hanh thông, và con sẽ hành động khôn ngoan và thành công.
vi.R: Hãy luôn luôn nói về lời dạy trong sách này. Hãy suy nghĩ về những lời ấy cả ngày lẫn đêm. Như vậy con sẽ cẩn thận làm theo mọi điều đã chép trong đó. Nếu con làm như thế, mọi việc con làm sẽ được tốt đẹp, và con sẽ hành động khôn ngoan và thành công.

ko.L: 이 율법책이 네 입에서 떠나지 않게 하고, 너는 낮이나 밤이나 그것을 읊조리며 묵상하여, 그 안에 기록된 모든 것을 따라 지켜 행하여라. 그러면 네 길을 형통하게 할 것이고, 그러면 네가 지혜롭게 행하게 될 것이다.
ko.B: 이 율법책의 말씀을 늘 입에 두고, 낮에도 밤에도 그것을 읊조리며 깊이 생각하여라. 그래서 그 안에 기록된 모든 것을 지켜 행하도록 조심하여라. 그러면 네 길이 잘 풀릴 것이고, 네가 지혜롭게 행하여 잘될 것이다.
ko.R: 이 책에 있는 가르침을 언제나 입으로 말하여라. 낮에도 밤에도 그것을 깊이 생각하여라. 그러면 그 책에 기록된 것을 모두 조심해서 지키게 될 것이다. 그렇게 하면 네가 하는 일이 잘되고, 네가 지혜롭게 행하여 성공할 것이다.

pt.L: Este livro da lei não se afastará da tua boca, e meditarás nele de dia e de noite, para que cuides de fazer conforme tudo o que nele está escrito; pois então tornarás prósperos os teus caminhos, e então agirás sabiamente e terás êxito.
pt.B: Tem sempre nos lábios este livro da lei e medita nele de dia e de noite, para que cuides de cumprir tudo o que nele está escrito. Então levarás os teus caminhos a bom termo, e então agirás com sabedoria e serás bem-sucedido.
pt.R: Fala sempre do ensino deste livro. Pensa nele de dia e de noite. Assim vais ter o cuidado de fazer tudo o que está escrito nele. Se fizeres isso, tudo o que fizeres vai dar certo, e vais agir com sabedoria e ter sucesso.

decisions.choice: this book of the law: the written instruction of Moses
decisions.reason: Moses wrote down "this law" and gave it to the priests and elders (Deuteronomy 31:9, 24-26), and the king was to keep a copy and read it all his life (Deuteronomy 17:18-19). "Law" here is the same word as in Deuteronomy 1:5: instruction, the whole of what Moses taught, not only its rules.

decisions.choice: will not depart from your mouth: you will keep speaking it
decisions.reason: Reading in the ancient world was usually done aloud. To have the book "in the mouth" is to keep reading and repeating its words, as Moses told Israel to talk about his words at home and on the road (Deuteronomy 6:7).

decisions.choice: meditate: murmur, repeat over quietly while thinking it through
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a low sound, a dove's moan or a lion's growl (Isaiah 31:4; 38:14). Here it means going over the words half aloud and turning them over in the mind. Psalm 1:2 uses the same words of the one who delights in the LORD's law.

decisions.choice: then you will make your ways prosper: success follows from keeping the law
decisions.reason: The repeated "then" puts the reward after the obedience. The first verb means to make something go well, to bring it to a good outcome; the second is the verb of verse 7, to act wisely and so succeed.

decisions.choice: Keep ... always on your lips / Always keep talking about
alternatives: shall not depart from your mouth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the negative statement into a positive command so the sense of the picture is plain. Readable says "teaching" for "law", as in Deuteronomy 1:5.

decisions.choice: "suy ngẫm" (L, B), "suy nghĩ về" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to murmur the words over while thinking them through (m3). "suy ngẫm" is the word Psalm 1:2 uses in this project; Readable uses the plainer "suy nghĩ về", and the first sentence, "luôn luôn nói", keeps the sense of saying the words aloud.

decisions.choice: "읊조리며 묵상하여라" (L), "읊조리며 깊이 생각하여라" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is to murmur or repeat quietly while thinking. "묵상" alone suggests silent thought, so the levels that keep the picture add "읊조리며" (reciting under the breath).

decisions.choice: meditarás (L), medita (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is a half-spoken going over of the words (m3). "Meditar" is the word Portuguese readers know from Psalm 1:2 for it; the speaking is already in "da tua boca" and "nos lábios", so the pair keeps both halves of the sense.

records.literal_gloss: [Have] not I commanded you? Be strong and be bold; do not tremble and do not be dismayed, for with you [is] Yahweh your God in all that you will go.

en.L: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and bold. Do not tremble, and do not be dismayed, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] with you wherever you go."
en.B: Have I not given you this command? Be strong and courageous. Do not tremble with fear or lose heart, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is with you wherever you go."
en.R: Remember, I am the one who gave you this command: Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or lose hope. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will be with you wherever you go."

sw.L: Je, si mimi niliyekuamuru? Uwe imara na jasiri. Usitetemeke wala usifadhaike, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako [yu] pamoja nawe kila mahali utakapokwenda."
sw.B: Je, sikukupa agizo hili? Uwe imara na jasiri. Usitetemeke kwa hofu wala usikate tamaa, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako yuko pamoja nawe kila mahali utakapokwenda."
sw.R: Kumbuka, mimi ndiye niliyekupa agizo hili: Uwe imara na shujaa. Usiogope wala usikate tamaa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakuwa pamoja nawe kila mahali utakapokwenda."

es.L: ¿No te lo he mandado yo? Sé fuerte y valeroso. No tiembles, y no te acobardes, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios [está] contigo dondequiera que vayas».
es.B: ¿No te he dado yo esta orden? Sé fuerte y valiente. No tiembles de miedo ni pierdas el ánimo, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios está contigo dondequiera que vayas».
es.R: Recuerda que yo soy quien te dio esta orden: Sé fuerte y valiente. No tengas miedo ni pierdas la esperanza. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios estará contigo dondequiera que vayas».

fr.L: Ne t’ai-je pas commandé : Sois fort et courageux ? Ne tremble pas et ne t’effraie pas, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu [est] avec toi partout où tu iras. »
fr.B: Ne t’ai-je pas donné cet ordre ? Sois fort et courageux. Ne tremble pas de peur et ne perds pas courage, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est avec toi partout où tu iras. »
fr.R: Souviens-toi : c’est moi qui t’ai donné cet ordre. Sois fort et courageux. N’aie pas peur et ne perds pas espoir. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu sera avec toi partout où tu iras. »

vi.L: Chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền lệnh cho ngươi sao? Hãy mạnh mẽ và dạn dĩ. Chớ run sợ và chớ kinh hãi, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi [ở] với ngươi bất cứ nơi nào ngươi đi."
vi.B: Chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền lệnh này cho con sao? Hãy mạnh mẽ và can đảm. Đừng run sợ, cũng đừng nản lòng, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của con ở với con bất cứ nơi nào con đi."
vi.R: Hãy nhớ rằng chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền lệnh này cho con: Hãy mạnh mẽ và dũng cảm. Đừng sợ hãi, cũng đừng mất hy vọng. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của con sẽ ở với con bất cứ nơi nào con đi."

ko.L: 내가 너에게 명령하지 않았느냐? 강하고 담대하여라. 떨지 말고 놀라지 마라. 네가 어디로 가든지 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 계신다."
ko.B: 내가 너에게 이렇게 명령하지 않았느냐? 강하고 담대하여라. 두려워 떨지 말고 낙심하지 마라. 네가 어디로 가든지 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 계신다."
ko.R: 기억하여라. 이 명령을 내린 이는 바로 나다. 힘을 내고 용기를 가져라. 두려워하지 말고 희망을 잃지 마라. 네가 어디로 가든지 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너와 함께 계실 것이다."

pt.L: Não te ordenei [eu]? Sê forte e corajoso. Não tremas e não te apavores, pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus, [está] contigo aonde quer que fores."
pt.B: Acaso não te dei esta ordem? Sê forte e corajoso. Não tremas de medo nem percas o ânimo, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus, está contigo aonde quer que fores."
pt.R: Lembra-te: fui eu que te dei esta ordem. Sê forte e corajoso. Não tenhas medo nem percas a esperança. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus, vai estar contigo aonde quer que fores."

decisions.choice: Have I not commanded you?: a question that expects "yes" and stresses who gives the order
decisions.reason: The question reminds Joshua that the charge to be strong comes from God himself, so it carries God's authority and his promise.

decisions.choice: tremble, be dismayed: be struck with terror, be broken in spirit
decisions.reason: The first verb means to shake with dread; the second to be shattered or lose heart. Moses used the same pair when he told Israel not to fear its enemies (Deuteronomy 1:21, 29; 31:6, 8).

decisions.choice: the LORD your God is with you: the reason Joshua need not fear
decisions.reason: The command rests on the promise of verse 5. Joshua's courage does not depend on his own strength but on God's presence, wherever he goes.

decisions.choice: Remember, I am the one who gave you this command
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question means instead of asking it, since a question that expects "yes" can confuse young readers.

decisions.choice: officials: officers who kept records and passed on orders
decisions.reason: This word names officers who served under leaders and judges: the Israelite foremen in Egypt (Exodus 5:14-19), helpers of the elders (Numbers 11:16), and the officers who spoke to the army before battle (Deuteronomy 20:5-9). Here they carry Joshua's orders through the camp.

decisions.choice: and Joshua commanded: Joshua acts at once on God's word
decisions.reason: The story moves straight from God's command to Joshua's first orders. The one who has just been commanded (verses 7, 9) now commands others.

decisions.choice: the officials who served the people
decisions.reason: Readable adds "who served" to show that these were officers among the people, not rulers over them.

decisions.choice: "maafisa"
decisions.reason: The shoterim kept records and passed on orders; "maafisa" (officials) says this without making them army commanders ("wakuu wa jeshi") or scribes only.

decisions.choice: "관리들" for the officials
decisions.reason: These were officers who kept records and passed on orders. "관리" is the plain modern word for an official; the older word is no longer understood.

decisions.choice: os oficiais (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 3:2; 8:33; 23:2; 24:1), as Deuteronomy 1:15 and 16:18 set it in Portuguese: the officers who kept records and passed on orders (m1) are "oficiais"; "supervisores" stays with the foremen of Exodus 5.

records.literal_gloss: Pass through [the] midst of the camp and command the people, saying, Prepare for yourselves provisions, for in yet three days you [are] crossing over the Jordan the this to go in to take possession of the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you to take possession of it.

en.L: "Pass through the midst of the camp and command the people, saying, 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, for within three days you are crossing over this Jordan, to go in to take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to possess it.'"
en.B: "Go through the camp and give the people this order: 'Get your food ready for the journey, because three days from now you will cross this Jordan to go in and take possession of the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as your own.'"
en.R: "Go through the camp and tell the people, 'Get food ready to take with you. In three days you will cross the Jordan River. You will go in and take the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to be your own.'"

sw.L: "Piteni katikati ya kambi, mkawaamuru watu, mkisema, 'Jiwekeeni tayari chakula cha njiani, kwa maana katika muda wa siku tatu mtavuka Yordani hii, ili kuingia kuimiliki nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anawapa ili kuimiliki.'"
sw.B: "Piteni katika kambi yote mkawape watu agizo hili: 'Andaeni chakula cha safari, kwa sababu siku tatu kuanzia leo mtavuka Yordani hii, ili mwingie kuimiliki nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anawapa iwe yenu.'"
sw.R: "Pitieni kambi nzima, mkawaambie watu, 'Tayarisheni chakula cha kuchukua njiani. Baada ya siku tatu mtavuka Mto Yordani. Mtaingia na kuichukua nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anawapa iwe yenu.'"

es.L: «{{plural_you:Pasen|Pasad}} por en medio del campamento y {{plural_you:manden|mandad}} al pueblo, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} provisiones para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque dentro de tres días {{plural_you:cruzarán|cruzaréis}} este Jordán, para entrar a tomar posesión de la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} da para que la {{plural_you:posean|poseáis}}”».
es.B: «{{plural_you:Recorran|Recorred}} el campamento y {{plural_you:den|dad}} al pueblo esta orden: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} la comida para el viaje, porque dentro de tres días {{plural_you:cruzarán|cruzaréis}} este Jordán para entrar y tomar posesión de la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} da como {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}”».
es.R: «{{plural_you:Recorran|Recorred}} el campamento y {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}} al pueblo: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} comida para llevar. Dentro de tres días {{plural_you:cruzarán|cruzaréis}} el río Jordán. {{plural_you:Entrarán|Entraréis}} y {{plural_you:tomarán|tomaréis}} la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} da para que sea {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}”».

fr.L: « Passez au milieu du camp et commandez au peuple, en disant : “Préparez-vous des provisions, car dans trois jours vous passerez ce Jourdain, pour aller prendre possession du pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous donne pour le posséder.” »
fr.B: « Parcourez le camp et donnez cet ordre au peuple : “Préparez vos provisions, car dans trois jours vous traverserez ce Jourdain pour aller prendre possession du pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous donne en propriété.” »
fr.R: « Allez dans tout le camp et dites au peuple : “Préparez de la nourriture à emporter. Dans trois jours, vous allez traverser le fleuve Jourdain. Vous entrerez dans le pays et vous le prendrez. C’est le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous donne pour qu’il soit à vous.” »

vi.L: "Hãy đi qua giữa trại quân và truyền lệnh cho dân rằng: 'Hãy chuẩn bị lương thực cho các ngươi, vì trong ba ngày nữa các ngươi sẽ đi qua sông Giô-đanh này, để vào chiếm hữu xứ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi đang ban cho các ngươi để chiếm hữu.'"
vi.B: "Hãy đi khắp trại quân và truyền cho dân lệnh này: 'Anh em hãy chuẩn bị lương thực cho chuyến đi, vì ba ngày nữa anh em sẽ đi qua sông Giô-đanh này, để vào chiếm hữu xứ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đang ban cho anh em làm của riêng.'"
vi.R: "Hãy đi khắp trại quân và nói với dân: 'Anh em hãy chuẩn bị thức ăn mang theo. Ba ngày nữa anh em sẽ đi qua sông Giô-đanh. Anh em sẽ vào chiếm lấy xứ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đang ban cho anh em làm của riêng.'"

ko.L: "진영 가운데로 두루 다니며 백성에게 명령하여 말하여라. '너희는 양식을 준비하여라. 삼 일 안에 너희가 이 요단을 건너, 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희에게 주셔서 차지하게 하시는 땅을 차지하러 들어갈 것이다.'"
ko.B: "진영을 두루 다니며 백성에게 이렇게 명령하여라. '길에서 먹을 양식을 준비하여라. 사흘 뒤에 너희는 이 요단강을 건너, 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희 소유로 주시는 땅에 들어가 그 땅을 차지할 것이다.'"
ko.R: "진영을 다니며 백성에게 말하여라. '가지고 갈 음식을 준비하여라. 사흘 뒤에 너희는 요단강을 건널 것이다. 너희는 들어가서, 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희 것으로 주시는 땅을 차지할 것이다.'"

pt.L: "Passem pelo meio do acampamento e ordenem ao povo, dizendo: 'Preparem provisões para vocês, pois dentro de três dias vocês atravessam este Jordão para entrar e tomar posse da terra que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, dá a vocês para possuí-la.'"
pt.B: "Percorram o acampamento e deem esta ordem ao povo: 'Preparem comida para a viagem, porque daqui a três dias vocês vão atravessar este Jordão para entrar e tomar posse da terra que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, está dando a vocês como propriedade.'"
pt.R: "Passem pelo acampamento e digam ao povo: 'Preparem comida para levar. Daqui a três dias vocês vão atravessar o rio Jordão. Vão entrar e tomar posse da terra que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, está dando a vocês para ser de vocês.'"

decisions.choice: provisions: food for a journey
decisions.reason: The word means food taken along on a journey (Genesis 42:25; Exodus 12:39). The manna was still coming each day and did not stop until Israel ate the produce of the land after crossing (5:11-12), so these provisions may be other food to carry across, or simply food made ready for the move.

decisions.choice: within three days: three days from now, a short, fixed time
decisions.reason: The phrase means "in three more days". In 3:2 the officials go through the camp "at the end of three days", and the spies' three days in hiding (2:22) may fall within the same time. "Three days" can be a round number for a short time, and the exact sequence of these days is not certain.

decisions.choice: take possession of: take over and hold as one's own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take land and hold it, often by driving out those who live there. It is used twice: Israel goes in to take the land, which God is giving them to hold.

decisions.choice: as your own / to be your own
decisions.reason: The second "to take possession of it" repeats the first. Balanced and Readable give its sense once more with "as your own" instead of repeating the verb.

decisions.choice: the people addressed as "anh em" (B, R); "các ngươi" (L)
decisions.reason: A leader speaking to the whole people of Israel calls them "anh em" (brothers and sisters, fellow members of the people), which is how Vietnamese speaks to an assembly of one's own people; Literal keeps the plain "các ngươi". Joshua and his officials address the people this way through chapters 1 to 12.

decisions.choice: "chiếm hữu" (L, B), "chiếm lấy ... làm của riêng" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over and hold as one's own (m3). "chiếm hữu" says both; Readable spells it out.

decisions.choice: Joshua gives orders to his officials, and through them to the people, in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: Joshua speaks as Israel's commander; the plain style is how a leader gives orders in Korean narrative. The people answer him in the formal polite style (verse 16).

decisions.choice: the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh: the tribes that settled east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: These two and a half tribes had asked for the land east of the Jordan, which was good for their herds, and Moses gave it to them on condition that their fighting men cross over and help the other tribes (Numbers 32; Deuteronomy 3:12-20).

decisions.choice: and to the Reubenites ...: the tribes are named first to set them apart
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the names before the verb, which marks a change of subject: Joshua now turns from all the people to these tribes in particular.

decisions.choice: the tribes of Reuben and Gad
decisions.reason: Readable names the tribes instead of using "Reubenites" and "Gadites", which are harder words for young readers.

decisions.choice: "les Rubénites", "les Gadites", "la demi-tribu de Manassé"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua 1-12: the usual French names for the two tribes and the half-tribe that settled east of the Jordan. Readable says "the tribes of Reuben and Gad" ("les tribus de Ruben et de Gad"), as the English does.

decisions.choice: os rubenitas, os gaditas, a meia tribo de Manassés (L, B); as tribos de Rúben e de Gade, a metade da tribo de Manassés (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as Numbers 32 and Deuteronomy 3:12-13 have it in Portuguese: "rubenitas" and "gaditas" and "a meia tribo de Manassés" (no hyphen) at Literal and Balanced; Readable names the tribes and says "a metade da tribo", as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: Remember the word which commanded you Moses, [the] servant of Yahweh, saying, Yahweh your God [is] giving rest to you, and he will give to you the land the this.

en.L: "Remember the word that Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you, saying, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you rest, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you this land.'
en.B: "Remember the command that Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave you: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you rest, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you this land.'
en.R: "Remember what Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, told you to do. He said, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you a place to rest. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will give you this land.'

sw.L: "Kumbukeni neno ambalo Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaamuru, akisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anawapa pumziko, naye atawapa nchi hii.'
sw.B: "Kumbukeni agizo ambalo Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa: '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anawapa pumziko, naye atawapa nchi hii.'
sw.R: "Kumbukeni yale ambayo Musa, mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliwaagiza. Alisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anawapa mahali pa kupumzika. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawapa nchi hii.'

es.B: «{{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} la orden que {{plural_you:les|os}} dio Moisés, siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} da reposo, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dará esta tierra”.
es.R: «{{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} lo que Moisés, el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} mandó hacer. Él dijo: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:les|os}} da un lugar donde descansar. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dará esta tierra”.

fr.L: « Souvenez-vous de la parole que vous a prescrite Moïse, serviteur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, en disant : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous donne du repos, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous donnera ce pays.”
fr.B: « Souvenez-vous de l’ordre que vous a donné Moïse, serviteur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous donne le repos, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous donnera ce pays.”
fr.R: « Souvenez-vous de ce que Moïse, le serviteur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, vous a dit de faire. Il a dit : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous donne un endroit où vous reposer. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous donnera ce pays.”

vi.B: "Hãy nhớ lệnh mà Môi-se, đầy tớ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đã truyền cho anh em: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đang ban cho anh em sự an nghỉ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ban cho anh em xứ này.'
vi.R: "Hãy nhớ điều Môi-se, đầy tớ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đã bảo anh em làm. Ông nói: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đang ban cho anh em một nơi để an nghỉ. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ ban cho anh em xứ này.'

ko.L: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 종 모세가 너희에게 명령하여 말한 그 말을 기억하여라. '너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희에게 안식을 주시고, 이 땅을 너희에게 주실 것이다.'
ko.B: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 종 모세가 너희에게 명령한 말을 기억하여라. '너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희에게 안식을 주시고, 이 땅을 너희에게 주실 것이다.'
ko.R: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 종 모세가 너희에게 하라고 한 말을 기억하여라. 모세가 말했다. '너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희에게 쉴 곳을 주신다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅을 너희에게 주실 것이다.'

pt.L: "Lembrem-se da palavra que Moisés, o escravo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, ordenou a vocês, dizendo: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, dá descanso a vocês, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dará a vocês esta terra.'
pt.B: "Lembrem-se da ordem que Moisés, o servo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, deu a vocês: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, está dando descanso a vocês, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dará a vocês esta terra.'
pt.R: "Lembrem-se do que Moisés, o servo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, mandou que vocês fizessem. Ele disse: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, está dando a vocês um lugar para descansar. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vai dar esta terra a vocês.'

decisions.choice: the word Moses commanded you: the agreement of Numbers 32 and Deuteronomy 3:18-20
decisions.reason: Joshua reminds the eastern tribes of the terms Moses set: they may have their land east of the Jordan, but their fighting men must cross ahead of the other tribes until those tribes too have rest and land (Numbers 32:20-32; Deuteronomy 3:18-20). He sums up Moses' words; he does not quote them exactly.

decisions.choice: giving you rest: a settled, secure life in the land, free from enemies
decisions.reason: Rest is God's promised gift once the land is won (Deuteronomy 3:20; 12:9-10; 25:19). The eastern tribes have it already; the others will have it when the land west of the Jordan is taken (verse 15; 21:44; 22:4).

decisions.choice: this land: the land east of the Jordan where the eastern tribes are
decisions.reason: "This land" is the land where Joshua and the tribes are standing, east of the river, which Moses had given them (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the servant of the LORD: Moses' title, as in verse 1
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the title marks Moses as the one who belonged to God and spoke for him.

decisions.choice: The LORD will give you
decisions.reason: Readable repeats "the LORD" in place of "he" at the start of a new short sentence, so it is clear who gives the land.

decisions.choice: "sự an nghỉ" (L, B), "một nơi để an nghỉ" (R)
decisions.reason: Rest here is a settled life in the land, safe from enemies (m2). Readable makes the place explicit, as the English Readable does.
